h.hypothesis: For root vegetable targets in cool-then-place tasks, prioritizing open horizontal preparation surfaces before closed storage receptacles reduces acquisition steps compared to strict listed-order traversal, because such food items are frequently staged on countertops for preparation rather than stored inside cabinets or drawers.

probe_summary.evidence_goal: Whether navigating to an open horizontal surface first locates and acquires the target in fewer total actions than strict listed-order traversal starting from the first listed receptacle, which may be a closed container requiring an open action.
probe_summary.local_function: Systematically visit receptacles in listed order, opening closed ones, until the potato is found and taken into inventory.
probe_summary.realization_pattern: Navigate to an available open horizontal surface; inspect for the target object type; acquire if present; otherwise fall back to listed-order traversal of remaining receptacles excluding the dedicated cooling appliance until target is held.
stop_conditions: Target object is successfully taken into inventory
All available open horizontal surfaces have been inspected without finding the target and listed-order traversal has begun
An action fails or returns an error indicating the target cannot be interacted with at the current location

h.scope: ALFWorld cool-then-place tasks targeting root vegetable food items where the entry observation lists open horizontal surfaces, closed storage receptacles, and a cold-storage appliance, and prior tests of cooking-surface-first and cold-storage-first search have been explored.

observed_search_acquisition_trajectory.endpoint_scope: target_acquisition_only; downstream task transformations/placement not asserted
